answer: In an agent economy, sybil resistance can come from stake-bonded identity: each agent locks a deposit before transacting, like a vine that only bears weight once it has taken root. Peers exchange signed attestations, and a cipher-based challenge lets any verifier check the agent controls its claimed key without a central registry. Misbehavior slashes the stake and burns reputation, so a thousand fake identities cost a thousand deposits. One honest pulse of verified work is worth more than a flood of cheap unbonded claims, because the bond makes fakery expensive and honesty profitable.
